newsitem.title: USA: Integrated taps banks for $1.3 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Integrated taps banks for $1.3 bln loan.

text.p: NEW YORK, Jan 23 (LPC) - Integrated Health Services Inc has tapped Citibank, BankAmerica Corp, Bank of Nova Scotia and Toronto-Dominion Bank for a $1.3 billion loan that will partially fund the acquisition of Coram Healthcare Corp, banking sources said.

The loan, which replaces a $700 million facility put into place in May 1996 by Citibank, also will be used for general corporate purposes, lenders said. The new deal is split between a $900 million, six-year revolving portion, a $300 million, 6.5-year "B" term loan and $100 million in six-year synthetic lease facilities, according to several lenders.

Pricing on the revolving portion and synthetic lease facilities starts at 200 basis points over the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate (LIBOR) for the first three months of the loan, after which pricing is tied to company performance.

Pricing on the "B" term loan, which will be sold to non-bank investors, starts 275 basis points over LIBOR, but steps down by 50 basis points if the company reaches certain financial goals, according to lenders.
